gist: Permanent settlement qualifying time for migrants increases from five to 10 years.
Shorter qualifying periods apply for high earners, care workers, and public service professionals.
Applicants must meet strict conditions regarding income, language, and no criminal record.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The government plans to double the standard length of time migrants must live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. A 10-year pathway requires earning at least £12,571 for five of the seven years before settlement. Shorter qualifying periods of three or five years apply to specific groups, including high earners, certain care workers, skilled public service workers, and people with British National (Overseas) status. Conversely, migrants who claimed certain benefits or breached rules face a 20-year wait. Additional conditions include having no criminal record, speaking good English, owing no taxpayer debt, and having a record of National Insurance contributions.
